addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

=== instruction.md ===
# Bug: in a collaborative session, carets and selections end up in the wrong place

The attached frames are from a two-pane collaborative session. Each pane's own debug panel,
underneath its editor, reports that pane's own live selection offset.

Further things break, independent of what the frames show. Another participant moving
their caret, selecting text, or leaving the session should be reflected every time it
happens; none of it is. An edit made earlier in the document leaves your own caret and selection behind,
on text they no longer belong on. And any position that is not simply so many characters
into a line -- a blank line, a paragraph edge, a selection that spans two paragraphs --
lands wrong.

100% reproducible in a two-pane collaborative session.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/bug_screenshot_1_1.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/bug_screenshot_1_2.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/bug_screenshot_1_3.png`
=== task.toml ===
version = "1.0"

[metadata]
task_id = "facebook__lexical-7959-mm"
title = "Bug: in a collaborative session, carets and selections end up in the wrong place"
repository_name = "facebook/lexical"
repo_url = "https://github.com/facebook/lexical"
issue_number = 7959
pr_number = 7960
base_commit = "34cab58e2ce3997d829ac7b68413fa0acf9c24dc"
fix_commit = "174580dfbb2d1a54fa0b102e7938407d9c8aca34"
task_type = "visual_bug_fix"
language = "TypeScript"
framework = "Lexical / React / vitest (unit, jsdom)"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "essential"
difficulty = "hard"
difficulty_explanation = """
The report gives only a symptom and a screen recording: in a collaborative session the text
replicates fine, but caret and selection positions end up wrong. Nothing throws, nothing logs,
and four independent defects across three files contribute to it.

1. `useYjsCollaboration` (packages/lexical-react/src/shared/useYjsCollaboration.tsx), the hook
   behind the main (non-experimental) `CollaborationPlugin`, never subscribes to the Yjs
   Awareness 'update' event, so cursor rendering re-runs only from the Yjs document
   tree-change listener -- which is why the reporter observed that the position after typing
   is still synced. This is the upstream regression PR #7960 fixes.

2. `syncCursorPositions` (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncCursors.ts) creates a remote cursor's
   selection the first time it sees a participant but never rewrites it, so a remote caret
   freezes at the first place it appeared.

3. `$syncCursorFromYjs` (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncEditorStates.ts) no longer re-derives
   the LOCAL editor's own selection from the relative position that client published, so a
   participant's own caret keeps a raw offset and drifts whenever somebody edits earlier
   content.

4. `createRelativePosition` (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncCursors.ts) encodes a STRUCTURAL
   (element) point -- the kind a caret has on a blank line or at a paragraph boundary -- the
   way a text point is encoded: against the PARENT's shared type at the element's own slot,
   rather than against the element's own shared type at the accumulated content offset of the
   child boundary. Consequence: a collaborator's caret on a blank line does not appear, a
   caret at the end of a paragraph is drawn in the NEXT paragraph, and a selection ending on a
   blank line has that end land in the wrong place.

Defects 1-3 are restoration-shaped: each has a working analogue within a screen or two (the v2
hook, the creation branch three lines up, the same helper call in the sibling branch), and a
prior trial repaired all three in about four minutes. Defect 4 is deliberately not of that
shape. The correct algorithm is REPLACED by a plausible wrong one rather than deleted, so
there is no adjacent line to copy; the v1 content-unit layout (a text child occupies 1 + length
units, any other child 1) has to be derived from the decode walk in Utils.ts and from the node
sizes, and the v2 encoder 30 lines below is a trap -- it counts children against the node's own
shared type, which is right for v2's layout and wrong for v1's. A candidate reproducing the
prior trial's three fixes exactly passes 11 of the 14 behavioural tests.
"""
files_edited = [
  "packages/lexical-react/src/shared/useYjsCollaboration.tsx",
  "packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncCursors.ts",
  "packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncEditorStates.ts",
]
f2p = [
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows a remote caret that appeared from a selection-only change, with no document edit",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > moves an already-visible remote caret to the position it moved to",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows both ends of a remote selection range, in the direction it was made",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > replaces a remote selection range with the new range, with no document edit",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > follows several consecutive remote selection changes with no typing in between",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps two remote participant selections independent of each other",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > stops showing a remote participant once they leave the session",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps following a remote participant selection after that participant typed",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps the local caret on the same text when a remote edit inserts before it",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps the local caret on the same text when a remote edit deletes before it",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps both ends of the local selection on the same text through a remote edit",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows a remote caret sitting on an empty line, on that line",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows a remote caret at the end of a paragraph in that paragraph",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows both ends of a remote selection that runs into another paragraph",
]
p2p = [
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > syncs plain document text between two participants",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > syncs a second, independent document edit after the first",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > keeps syncing document text after several selection-only changes",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > resumes document sync after a participant disconnects and reconnects",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows a remote caret that arrives together with a document update",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > leaves the local caret alone when a remote edit lands after it",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > shows ordinary text positions correctly across paragraphs",
  "packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx > Collaboration: remote participant caret and selection state > never shows a participant their own caret, and tracks exactly the others",
]
tags = ["multimodal", "visual_bug_fix"]
